subject: Culture
title: Earth Day's Beginnings
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Earth Day's Beginnings.

hook.text: Earth Day began in 1970 because a senator saw an oil spill and a campus protest—and connected them.

buildup.text: Senator Gaylord Nelson organized teach-ins across US universities. Twenty million people participated.

discovery.text: Earth Day led directly to the EPA, the Clean Air Act, and the Clean Water Act. One day changed US law.

twist.text: Critics say Earth Day became corporate greenwashing. Companies sponsor it while polluting year-round.

climax.text: A festival created to demand change risks becoming the thing that lets people feel good without changing.

punchline.text: One day of awareness can launch a movement or replace one.

quiz.question: What major US agency was created as a result of the first Earth Day?
